prompt.text:
Implement an in-memory artifact catalog in package `solution`.

Export:

```go
type Artifact struct {
    Workspace string
    Namespace string
    Alias     string
    URI       string
    Digest    string
}
type Lookup struct {
    URI       string
    Workspace string
    Namespace string
    Alias     string
}
type Catalog struct { /* unexported fields */ }
var ErrInvalidArtifact error
var ErrInvalidLookup error
var ErrNotFound error
func NewCatalog() *Catalog
func (c *Catalog) Put(a Artifact) error
func (c *Catalog) Get(q Lookup) (Artifact, error)
func (c *Catalog) Delete(workspace, namespace, alias string) error
func (c *Catalog) List(offset, limit int) ([]Artifact, error)
func (c *Catalog) Count() int
```

`Put` requires non-empty `Workspace`, `Namespace`, and `Alias`, plus at least one of `URI` or `Digest`. The tuple `(Workspace, Namespace, Alias)` is the identity; putting it again replaces all stored fields. `Get` accepts exactly one lookup form: a non-empty `URI` with all tuple fields empty, or a complete tuple with `URI` empty. Any other combination returns `ErrInvalidLookup`. URI lookup returns `ErrNotFound` when zero or multiple artifacts have that URI. `Delete` requires a complete tuple and returns `ErrNotFound` if absent. `List` rejects negative arguments, sorts by `Workspace`, then `Namespace`, then `Alias`, and returns at most `limit` entries beginning at `offset`. A zero limit returns an empty non-nil slice; an offset at or beyond the count does likewise. Returned slices must not expose catalog storage. A nil receiver behaves like an empty catalog for `Count`, `Get`, `Delete`, and `List`; mutation through `Put` returns `ErrInvalidArtifact`. Strings are compared exactly without normalization. Provide a complete standard-library-only source file.
